title: Forbidden City sold out? A stupa from 1279 is your Plan B | China Travel Expert
description:
Flying to Beijing for the Forbidden City? Here's the thing that catches people out — and the walk-up Plan B when it happens.

The Palace Museum sells NO same-day tickets. Every day's timed, real-name tickets go online seven days ahead at 8:00 pm Beijing time, tied to your passport, and popular dates can vanish in minutes (the site is capped around 40,000 visitors a day, and it's closed on Mondays). Miss the window and there's no gate window to save you.

So here's the Plan B, about 3 km west: the White Stupa of Miaoying Temple (妙应寺白塔). It was designed by the Nepali architect Araniko for Kublai Khan and dates to 1279 — the oldest and largest Tibetan-style stupa in China, and the main surviving relic of Yuan-dynasty Dadu. Admission is only about ¥20, and you just walk up. (Don't confuse it with Beihai Park's White Dagoba, which is a different, later stupa from 1651.)

🧭 Expert Tip: book the Forbidden City the moment the 8pm window opens, seven days out — and keep the White Stupa and nearby hutongs as your backup day. Never plan the Forbidden City for a Monday.

故宫不卖当天票：每天的分时实名票提前7天晚上8点放，凭护照入场，热门日期几分钟售罄，周一闭馆。没抢到怎么办？往西约3公里就是妙应寺白塔——元代1279年、尼泊尔工匠阿尼哥为忽必烈设计，中国现存最早最大的藏式佛塔，门票约20元，走着就能进。（别和北海白塔1651年那座搞混。）
